Write a provenance receipt

Source: R/crt_receipt_write.R
crt_receipt_write.Rd

Writes receipt.json for one output: what it is, how it was made, what came out, and where and when. The package supplies the values it knows; this function computes everything that must agree byte for byte across implementations: the recipe_id, each table's fingerprint, each part's size and SHA-256, and the config files' SHA-256 (crate#43).

Usage

crt_receipt_write(
  dir,
  output,
  recipe,
  result = list(),
  context = list(),
  keys = NULL,
  lockfile = NULL,
  publish = FALSE,
  file = "receipt.json"
)

Arguments

dir

Directory to write receipt.json into: the output's directory. parts are relative to it.

output, recipe, result, context

Named lists, one per block (see above).

keys

Optional: the package's declaration, from crt_receipt_keys(). When given, the tolerances come from it and the inputs, settings, config files and tables supplied must be exactly those it declares.

lockfile

Path to a lockfile whose SHA-256 is recorded in context, or NULL. Defaults to renv.lock in the working directory when one exists.

publish

TRUE for a receipt that will be published: leaves the host out.

file

The receipt's file name inside dir: a bare name ending .json, with no path separator, so the receipt sits in the directory its parts are relative to. Name it after the output ("CH_rear_grades_receipt.json") where several outputs share a directory; the name is not part of the receipt (#47). A name that resolves to a file the receipt hashes (a part, a config file, the lockfile) is refused, since writing the receipt would replace those bytes.

Value

The SHA-256 of the bytes written, as 64 lower-case hex digits, invisibly. The file is file.path(dir, file); read it with crt_receipt_read(). The digest is what a STAC item's receipt asset carries as file:checksum (crt_receipt_stac()): nothing else can compute it, since a receipt's own bytes are not inside it, and taking it here means the caller never re-reads the file and risks hashing another version of it (#60).

The blocks

  • output: name, and optionally scope (the partition: a watershed group, a region) and schema (the crate schema the output conforms to).

  • recipe: code, a list keyed by repository of list(commit, version, dirty), with commit the full 40-character SHA; config, a list of files (paths, hashed here; named to set the key, otherwise keyed by the path as given) and settings (the resolved run settings, written verbatim: wrap a length-one vector in I() to keep it an array). A config file is hashed as its bytes, as checked out: a repo whose config enters recipe_id should pin its line endings (.gitattributes: *.yaml text eol=lf), or a CRLF checkout is another recipe; inputs, keyed by input name, each exactly one of list(recipe_id = ), list(version_id = ), list(sha256 = ) or list(none = "why"); and seed, an integer or NULL.

  • result: tables, a named list of data frames to fingerprint; parts, the output's files as paths relative to dir, each named by the table it holds where it holds one (c(access_check = "access_check.csv", "map.tif")), so a comparison can tell a file whose bytes moved within its table's tolerance from one that changed; summary, named numbers such as rows or km_total; and tolerance, list(tables = list(<table> = list(<column> = 1e-9)), summary = list(<name> = 1e-6)).

  • context: anything of run (identifiers), session, inputs (each input's own result, for reporting), toolchain and time. time defaults to now, in UTC; toolchain is filled with R's version and, when loaded, GDAL's, terra's, sf's and arrow's, and entries given here win. The host is recorded unless publish = TRUE.

Toolchain versions and every other part of context are never part of an identity: a GDAL upgrade alone leaves recipe_id unchanged, and the comparison decides from the result whether the output still agrees.

See also

crt_receipt_read(), crt_receipt_validate(), crt_receipt_compare(), crt_table_fingerprint().

Examples

dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "evidence")
dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
access <- data.frame(segment = c("s1", "s2"), km = c(12.3456789012, 7.25))
write.csv(access, file.path(dir, "access_check.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

digest <- crt_receipt_write(
  dir,
  output = list(name = "link_evidence", scope = "BULK"),
  recipe = list(
    code = list(link = list(commit = strrep("a", 40), version = "0.31.2", dirty = FALSE)),
    config = list(settings = list(species = I("CO"))),
    inputs = list(fwa = list(version_id = "3HL4kqtJlcpXroDTDmJ"))
  ),
  result = list(
    tables = list(access_check = access),
    parts = c(access_check = "access_check.csv"),
    summary = list(rows = 2L, km_total = sum(access$km)),
    tolerance = list(tables = list(access_check = list(km = 1e-9)),
                     summary = list(km_total = 1e-6))
  ),
  publish = TRUE
)
digest
#> [1] "d90ceec698177bdc07ad7f7f0c951e61da829bd339898eb4799a55c8cb2b621a"
crt_receipt_read(dir)$recipe$recipe_id
#> [1] "b61eb32306d67d8bcef8c87fed32aeff3681251bb70464956787675e901cd09b"
